item.title: NIPS ends boat mishap recovery
item.description: A 48-hour extended recovery operation by the New Ireland disaster office will conclude today, though local communities are on alert for any further sightings. The New Ireland Provincial Government on Sunday handed over six more bodies in Kavieng, bringing the total number of repatriated victims to 13, while 14 others remain missing at sea.
item.content:encoded:
A 48-hour extended recovery operation by the New Ireland disaster office will conclude today, though local communities are on alert for any further sightings.

The New Ireland Provincial Government on Sunday handed over six more bodies in Kavieng, bringing the total number of repatriated victims to 13, while 14 others remain missing at sea.

During the official handover ceremony, New Ireland Governor Byron Chan, accompanied by Provincial Administrator Richard Andia and New Ireland Provincial Disaster Coordinator, Terence Tasia, formally handed over the bodies to East New Britain Governor Michael Marum.

Governor Chan conveyed his deepest condolences on behalf of the people of New Ireland and said the province stands with East New Britain during this difficult time. He also assured the province of New Ireland's support and said it is ready to help whenever disaster strikes.

To support relief and custom protocols, the New Ireland Provincial Executive Council presented East New Britain with K70,000 in financial assistance alongside traditional shell money [mis], delivered by chief executive officer of Economic Sector Edward Lasisi.

Accepting the assistance, Governor Marum thanked the people and volunteers of New Ireland for handling the deceased with immense dignity, respect and care.

Marum presented K10,000 directly to the local search and rescue volunteers, promising a formal thank you ceremony once all recovery efforts and formal proceedings conclude.

The tragic boat accident happened on Saturday, July 18, in East New Britain waters, where 27 lives were claimed.

According to New Ireland Provincial Disaster Coordinator, Terence Tasia, the first five bodies were recovered in the Tigak group of islands on Wednesday, July 22. Four more were found in the same area on Thursday, and a teenager's body was recovered on Salapiu Island on Friday, July 25. Three female bodies were among those recovered off Djaul Island.

item.title: East Sepik cocoa farmers receive organic fertilizers to boost production
item.description: Cocoa farmers across East Sepik Province are taking another step towards increasing cocoa production following the rollout of an organic fertilizer distribution program supported by the East Sepik Governor's Office and the Cocoa Board of Papua New Guinea. The distribution of Ferti-Bio, an organic fertilizer approved by the PNG Cocoa Board to improve soil nutrients and enhance cocoa yields, commenc
item.content:encoded:
Cocoa farmers across East Sepik Province are taking another step towards increasing cocoa production following the rollout of an organic fertilizer distribution program supported by the East Sepik Governor's Office and the Cocoa Board of Papua New Guinea.

The distribution of Ferti-Bio, an organic fertilizer approved by the PNG Cocoa Board to improve soil nutrients and enhance cocoa yields, commenced at Hawain on 22 July 2026.

A total of 320 five-kilogram bags of Ferti-Bio were distributed during the first phase of the program to cocoa farmers representing all six districts of East Sepik Province.

Before the distribution, officers from the Cocoa Board of PNG conducted a practical training session to educate farmers on the correct application of the fertilizer to maximize its effectiveness and improve cocoa productivity.

East and West Sepik Regional Cocoa Board Manager Daryll Worimo, who officiated at the training and distribution, said the initiative comes at a critical time as global demand for Papua New Guinea cocoa continues to grow.

Worimo said increasing cocoa production is essential for farmers to take advantage of expanding international markets.

"With international demand for PNG cocoa increasing, it is vital for our farmers to increase production to meet that demand. The support from East Sepik Governor Allan Bird through the provision of Ferti-Bio is timely and will help farmers improve their cocoa yields," Worimo said.

He encouraged all cocoa farmers to participate in the training sessions before applying the fertilizer to ensure it is used correctly and delivers the intended results.

Meanwhile, Officer-in-Charge of the Smart Cocoa Program under the East Sepik Governor's Office, Ephraim Wango, assured farmers that the distribution would be carried out fairly across the province.

"No farmer will be left behind. From Hawain, the distribution team will move to Angoram, Maprik and other central locations to ensure the fertilizer is distributed evenly to all cocoa farmers," Mr. Wango said.

The initiative forms part of ongoing efforts by the East Sepik Governor’s office and the Cocoa Board of Papua New Guinea to strengthen cocoa production, improve farmers' incomes, and position East Sepik as one of the country's leading cocoa-producing provinces.

item.title: Queen of Paradise Orchestra students embark on international music journey
item.description: Two pioneering students from the Queen of Paradise Orchestra in Vanimo are set to begin an exciting new chapter in their musical journey after being accepted to study classical music in the Philippines. Domitila Aidan and Margela Wasemo were officially farewelled during a small ceremony before departing for St. Scholastica's College of Music in the Philippines, where they will undertake a two-year
item.content:encoded:
Two pioneering students from the Queen of Paradise Orchestra in Vanimo are set to begin an exciting new chapter in their musical journey after being accepted to study classical music in the Philippines.

Domitila Aidan and Margela Wasemo were officially farewelled during a small ceremony before departing for St. Scholastica's College of Music in the Philippines, where they will undertake a two-year diploma program in classical music.

The opportunity marks a major milestone not only for the two students but also for the Queen of Paradise Orchestra, which has grown into one of Papua New Guinea's most successful youth classical music programs.

For Domitila, who joined the orchestra in 2021 at just 15 years of age, the opportunity is both exciting and overwhelming.

She said while travelling overseas for the first time is a daunting experience, she is determined to complete her studies and return home to help teach and inspire future generations of young musicians in West Sepik.

Established in 2018 by the Institute of the Incarnate Word [IVE] Missionaries under the direction of Venezuelan musician Jesus Briceno, the Queen of Paradise Orchestra began with fewer than ten students.

Today, the program has grown to more than 150 young musicians, offering junior music education and developing what is now one of Papua New Guinea's few community-based symphonic orchestras.

Head of Orchestra program, Fr. Martin Prado, described the students' departure as an important achievement for the orchestra and a reflection of years of dedication by students, parents, teachers and supporters.

He said the long-term vision is to build local capacity by training Papua New Guineans to become qualified music educators and conductors who can continue expanding the program across West Sepik and eventually other parts of the country.

The students will receive professional training in classical music and conducting before returning to Vanimo to help lead and mentor the next generation of musicians.

Domitila's father, Aidan Namban, thanked the IVE Missionaries and everyone involved in the orchestra for giving his daughter an opportunity that he said has transformed her life.

He said the program has provided discipline, confidence and purpose, while opening doors that once seemed impossible.

The two students are scheduled to depart for the Philippines this week, marking another significant milestone for the Queen of Paradise Orchestra as it continues using music to empower young people and create educational opportunities for the future.

item.title: 18th Sepik River Crocodile and Arts Festival returns to Ambunti
item.description: The people of Ambunti in East Sepik are preparing to welcome visitors and participants as the 18th Sepik River Crocodile and Arts Festival returns to the district from 5th to 7th August, celebrating one of Papua New Guinea's most iconic cultural events. Held annually in the Ambunti-Drekikir district, the festival showcases the rich cultural heritage of the Sepik people through traditional performa
item.content:encoded:
The people of Ambunti in East Sepik are preparing to welcome visitors and participants as the 18th Sepik River Crocodile and Arts Festival returns to the district from 5th to 7th August, celebrating one of Papua New Guinea's most iconic cultural events.

Held annually in the Ambunti-Drekikir district, the festival showcases the rich cultural heritage of the Sepik people through traditional performances, cultural ceremonies, canoe racing, arts and crafts exhibitions, music, and the famous crocodile skin-cutting traditions that have made the province internationally renowned.

The three-day festival is expected to attract local and international tourists, cultural enthusiasts, artists, and business representatives eager to experience the unique customs and artistic traditions that have been preserved for generations along the mighty Sepik River.

Festival Committee Secretary Jacob Marek has appealed to the people of East Sepik to extend their traditional hospitality to the many international and local visitors expected to attend this year's festival. Marek urged communities to respect all tourists and guests throughout the three-day event, saying their experience in Ambunti would help promote the festival and the province as a premier cultural tourism destination.

"We encourage our people to welcome our visitors with respect and kindness. Many of our guests are travelling from overseas and other parts of Papua New Guinea to experience our unique culture. Let us show them the true Sepik spirit of hospitality and ensure they return home with positive memories of our province," Marek said.

He also called on participating cultural groups, vendors, transport operators, accommodation providers, and the general public to work together in maintaining a safe, clean, and peaceful environment during the celebrations.

The Sepik River Crocodile and Arts Festival has become one of Papua New Guinea's premier cultural tourism events, promoting the preservation of indigenous traditions while creating economic opportunities for local communities through tourism, hospitality, and the sale of authentic cultural products.

item.title: Water shutdown confirmed for this weekend
item.description: The anticipated partial shutdown of water supply into Port Moresby, is now confirmed to take place over the weekend, from Friday, July 31 at 10pm to 3am on Sunday, August 2. Water PNG Chief Executive Officer, James Young, in a statement, said the repair work was deferred earlier, because Water PNG needed time to undertake extensive remedial work, and also acquire materials to shorten the shutdown
item.content:encoded:
The anticipated partial shutdown of water supply into Port Moresby, is now confirmed to take place over the weekend, from Friday, July 31 at 10pm to 3am on Sunday, August 2.

Water PNG Chief Executive Officer, James Young, in a statement, said the repair work was deferred earlier, because Water PNG needed time to undertake extensive remedial work, and also acquire materials to shorten the shutdown period to just 29 hours, and not the usual one week.

He said that though the situation remains serious, Water PNG was able to stabilize the situation, by utilising their local engineers and some experts from around the world, to shorten the repair work time, and also prepare for a catastrophic failure during the repairs.

Young also added that the delay in the repair work, has resulted in the city losing about 10 million litres of water each day, through that major leak.

He also said that the partial shutdown, will also reduce the city's water supply from 100 million to 80 million litres per day, and this is undertaken to reduce impacts on households, so residential areas have more access to supplies on Saturday.

Young further added that the longest outage will be experienced in the downtown area, because this is where hotels and houses have the capacity to store water, unlike suburbs and settlements.

The Water PNG CEO, however urged everyone to store enough water, regardless of where they are living, to avoid any issues.

item.title: Timini Primary School opens K50,000 double classroom
item.description: Timini Primary School in the Mumeng local level government of Bulolo District officially opened a new K50,000 double classroom last week, becoming the fourth of 33 primary schools in the district to complete the infrastructure project. The double classroom was funded through a K50,000 allocation provided to each school in the district last year by the Bulolo District Development Authority [DDA] bo
item.content:encoded:
Timini Primary School in the Mumeng local level government of Bulolo District officially opened a new K50,000 double classroom last week, becoming the fourth of 33 primary schools in the district to complete the infrastructure project.

The double classroom was funded through a K50,000 allocation provided to each school in the district last year by the Bulolo District Development Authority [DDA] board to upgrade local learning facilities.

Bulolo MP Sam Basil Junior commended the school administration and community for their dedication in successfully delivering the building on time.

"Funds were distributed equally at K50,000 to all primary and secondary schools across the district to construct double classrooms," Basil Jr. said. "Timini Primary School is among the first to successfully complete its project."

The local MP said while some schools face logistical and geographical challenges that may delay construction, the DDA remains committed to supporting all project sites.

The official opening ceremony was attended by Basil Jr., members of the Bulolo DDA board, district and provincial education officials, ward councillors, community leaders, staff, students, and local residents.

Bulolo District Education Services Zone One Inspector, Wesley Rapish, emphasized that upgrading infrastructure directly impacts student outcomes and regional growth.

"The DDA is prioritizing education to build a strong human resource base for both local and national development," Rapish said.

He urged students to take pride in the new facilities and show their appreciation through hard work and academic performance.

Timini Primary School headteacher Samson Wangi expressed gratitude to the district leadership, noting that the DDA has provided nearly K100,000 in total financial support to the school.

"The new classroom was built from the initial K50,000 grant, with an additional support of nearly K50,000 provided to assist with other ongoing developments on campus," Wangi said.

In addition to the new double classroom, the DDA has committed to completing an unfinished classroom on site and funding a new multipurpose hall for the school.

Malangta Primary School in the Watut-Rural LLG is scheduled to open its new double classroom later this week, with several other schools across Bulolo District expected to follow soon.

item.title: Rosso’s Immigration legacy: Passport backlog cleared, borders strengthened
item.description: Deputy Prime Minister John Rosso has left the Immigration and Border Security Ministry after delivering major reforms, which include clearing the passport backlog, expanding immigration services across the country and introducing new digital systems. Mr Rosso officially handed over the ministry to the new Minister for Immigration, William Bando, on Wednesday, July 22.
item.content:encoded:
Deputy Prime Minister John Rosso has left the Immigration and Border Security Ministry after delivering major reforms, which include clearing the passport backlog, expanding immigration services across the country and introducing new digital systems.

Mr Rosso officially handed over the ministry to the new Minister for Immigration, William Bando, on Wednesday, July 22.

When Rosso took over Immigration ministry in October 2022, one of the biggest challenges was the large number of delayed passport applications and a shortage of passport books caused by the COVID-19 pandemic.

He said the government worked with the passport manufacturer to secure more passport books and speed up processing.

“Today, there is no backlog,” Mr Rosso said.

During his three years and nine months, Mr Rosso said the authority had made major improvements.

“We’ve accomplished a great deal in a short time. We’re not where we want to be yet, but we’re certainly not where we used to be,” he said.

Under his leadership, ICSA set up offices in Mt Hagen and Kokopo to provide regional services. New offices were also established in Arawa, Motukea International Sea Port, Rabaul Sea Port, Kiunga, Tabubil and Nadzab Tomodachi International Airport in Lae.

Mr Rosso said the opening of the Passport Printing Office at the Momase Regional Office in Lae was one of the key achievements of his term.

He said people from the Momase region, Highlands and parts of the New Guinea Islands could now access passport services closer to home instead of travelling to Port Moresby.

ICSA also improved visa services by reintroducing visa auto-grant processing, expanding online visa applications and increasing Visa-on-Arrival access for more countries.

Mr Rosso said these changes helped promote tourism, trade and investment in Papua New Guinea.

The authority also strengthened its international services, with migration officers appointed to PNG diplomatic missions in countries including China, Australia, Malaysia, Indonesia, India and the Philippines.

Mr Rosso highlighted technology upgrades as another major achievement, including the introduction of the new PNG e-passport with improved security features in 2025.

ICSA also launched the Sponsor Portal, allowing companies to apply online for work permits and working resident visas.

The introduction of the PNG Digital Arrival Card replaced the old paper arrival card, allowing travellers to complete arrival information online before travelling.

The Immigration Operations Command Centre was also established in Port Moresby in 2025 to strengthen immigration intelligence and border monitoring.

Mr Rosso also took a tough approach against foreigners who breached PNG’s immigration laws.

He said more than 500 illegal foreign nationals had been removed from the country during his time as minister for activities including illegal work, illegal businesses and other breaches of visa conditions.

“We welcome foreigners and their business, trade and investment to PNG, but they must follow our laws,” he said.

Mr Rosso also re-established the Citizenship Advisory Committee to address delays in citizenship applications.

The committee helped clear a backlog of applications, including cases involving West Papuans who have lived in PNG for many years.

He also directed a review of immigration laws, including the Citizenship Act, to address issues affecting Papua New Guineans who lost citizenship while working or studying overseas.

Mr Rosso thanked Chief Migration Officer Wellington Navasivu, senior officers and all ICSA staff for their support during his time as minister.

With Mr Bando now taking over the ministry, he inherits an immigration authority that has undergone major changes in services, technology and border management under Mr Rosso’s leadership.

item.title: Solo triumphs in penalty shoot out to qualify for U17 World Cup
item.description: The Solomon Islands have qualified for FIFA U-17 World Cup 2027, coming from behind to defeat Papua New Guinea on penalties at the PNG Football Stadium in Port Moresby. Henry Fa'arodo's side found themselves on the back foot for long stages of their third place play-off at OFC U-16 Men's Championship 2026, but found a way to rescue victory from the jaws of defeat, ripping a World Cup spot away fro
item.content:encoded:
The Solomon Islands have qualified for FIFA U-17 World Cup 2027, coming from behind to defeat Papua New Guinea on penalties at the PNG Football Stadium in Port Moresby.

Henry Fa'arodo's side found themselves on the back foot for long stages of their third place play-off at OFC U-16 Men's Championship 2026, but found a way to rescue victory from the jaws of defeat, ripping a World Cup spot away from Papua New Guinea with a late equaliser and four classy spot kicks in the penalty shootout.

The win sends the Solomon Islands through to their second FIFA U-17 World Cup, and their first in eight years, after previously qualifying for the tournament in 2019. It is also their highest finish at an OFC U-16 Men's Championship since hosting the competition in 2018.

It was Papua New Guinea and their striker Boas Tommy who spurned the best chances of a goalless first half. Twice Tommy fluffed his lines, almost running straight into the waiting arms of goalkeeper Eddie Aefi after being played in-behind.

Attempting to qualify for a maiden FIFA U-17 World Cup, the nerves were evident from the tournament hosts. They had the woodwork in their way when a long-raking free kick delivery ricocheted off the crossbar with the help of the gloves of Aefi, before defender Bomecge Basananuc had a header cleared off the goal-line from the following corner.

Ultimately the pressure told though, and it was captain Matthew Sopo who provided the breakthrough for Papua New Guinea in the 66th minute. The midfielder was first to pounce on a loose ball at the top of the box, driving a superb first-time effort into the top-left corner of the net on his right foot.

It looked as Sopo’s goal might prove decisive, but despite having been outplayed for the majority of the contest, the Solomon Islands mustered a miraculous equaliser to send the third place play-off to a penalty shoot-out with six minutes of normal time to play. PNG goalkeeper Luther Rodney failed to keep hold of a routine delivery in the box, allowing Andriano Kabolo to scramble the ball into the goal in the 84th minute.

The Solomon Islands had lost on penalties to Fiji in the semi-final, but held their nerve better on this occasion, profiting on two missed spot kicks from Papua New Guinea to book their World Cup tickets.

George Lea'i slotted the winning penalty, sparking emotional scenes on both sides, as Papua New Guinea fell crestfallen whilst those in Solomon Islands colours celebrated their place at the World Cup in Qatar next year.
